clue.text: Naughty boy keeping eagle's last brood in an unhealthy condition

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the boy letters enclose the rest
a naughty boy misbehaves, so the letters of the word boy are knocked out of order
with eagle's, last asks for the final letter of the bird's name

parts.note: the bird's name, whose final letter is taken
to brood is to sit on eggs, as a hen does

explanation.surface: A misbehaving boy cooped up with a brooding eagle chick, in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brood' is a verb here, what a hen does on her eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess body fat to a degree that harms health is a recognised medical condition.

clue.text: Insect on animal's a source of annoyance

parts.note: a bug is an insect
a bear is an animal

explanation.surface: A beetle crawling on a bear is irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate: something that persistently irritates or worries someone.

clue.text: Clean close to aisle in upturned seats

indicators.note: in puts the aisle's end letter inside the overturned seats
in a down light upturned means written bottom to top, so the seats word reads backwards

parts.note: pews are church benches

indicators.note: close to here means the end of, giving the last letter of aisle

explanation.surface: Tidy up the church, near the aisle, among the upended pews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' reverses PEWS to SWEP; E goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep is to clean a floor with a broom.

clue.text: Joint favourite team

parts.note: top as in top choice or best-loved
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Shared favourite among the teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective, shared; it is a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean cut of beef from the inside of the leg, sold as a roasting joint.

clue.text: Swaggering hitman accepting promotion

definitions.note: used as a noun here: swaggering is boastful show of boldness

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the hitman's word holds the promotion

parts.note: a bravo is a hired assassin or thug
an ad (advertisement) promotes a product

explanation.surface: A cocky contract killer takes a step up in his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bravo' is an old word for a hired killer, not the cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a loud, boastful display of daring meant to impress others.

clue.text: Book by Royal Society featuring old fellow

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the society's letters contain the others

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A volume from the Royal Society about an elderly scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's Epistle to the Romans is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: All-purpose taser shot into base

indicators.note: into places the scrambled letters inside the word for base

parts.note: base means low and vile

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters of taser are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stun gun fired at a low target can do anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' makes ERSAT from the stun gun's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to serve many uses or functions, adaptable to every job.

clue.text: Proper Liberal went first and fought for his honour

parts.note: due means proper or fitting, as in due care
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A decent Liberal took the lead and defended his reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentlemen once settled insults to honour by a formal fight with pistols or swords.

clue.text: Actor's dream bringing trouble

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters of dream bringing are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A performer's fantasy causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor's' gives the definition and 'is'; the Swedish star of Casablanca was an actress, called an actor here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish film star of Casablanca and Notorious, a Hollywood leading lady.

clue.text: Monster interrupting progress

indicators.note: the answer breaks into the middle of the word progress, sitting within its letters

explanation.surface: A beast that holds up advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale giant who eats people is the classic monster.

clue.text: Animal in popular end of cattle market bought by writer

indicators.note: items bought by someone end up held by them, so the writer encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word cattle

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A writer buys a fashionable creature at the tail end of a livestock sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bought by' signals containment: what is bought ends up in the buyer's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-climbing member of the weasel family found in European forests.

clue.text: Prince entering capital city of ancient Greece

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the prince goes inside the capital

parts.note: Delhi is the capital region of India

explanation.surface: A royal arrives in the capital of an ancient Greek city-state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks part of the definition, but the definition is 'city of ancient Greece'; 'capital' gives DELHI.
explanation.definitionFit: The site of the famous oracle of Apollo, a sacred town in classical Greece.

clue.text: Enter lab for training that's available for hire

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters of enter lab are put through a new order

explanation.surface: Go into the laboratory to train, a facility you can rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be let or leased out for a fee.

clue.text: Result during soccer replay causing increase in noise

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another, so the result sits within the soccer letters
a replay is the match played again, so the letters of soccer are rearranged

parts.note: an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: The scoreline in a cup replay makes the crowd roar louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replay' makes CRESCO from the sport's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for a gradual rise in volume, also used for any building swell of sound.

clue.text: Shed on island given to family for Jack Straw?

parts.note: to spill is to shed, as in shed or spill blood
kin means family

explanation.surface: A shed on an island handed to relatives for a former Home Secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was a British Labour minister; here a jackstraw is a thin stick in the pick-up-sticks game, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackstraw and this are both names for the small sticks lifted one at a time in pick-up-sticks.

clue.text: Writer's wife managed deli

indicators.note: managed can mean handled or arranged, so the letters of deli are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author's spouse ran a delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' makes ILDE from the shop's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar of that surname was an Irish playwright and wit, author of The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: Credit given to adult in charge of a good time

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
A was the film certificate for adult viewing

explanation.surface: Credit extended to a grown-up running the party.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish word for fun, lively talk and enjoyable company.

clue.text: Attention surrounding vehicle turning up for daily grind

indicators.note: in a down light turning up means read from bottom to top, reversing the whole assembly
surrounding means the attention word goes round the vehicle

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention
a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Noticing the car about to roll over, part of the everyday slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' builds ECARTAR, and 'turning up' reverses all of it, not just the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitive, wearying routine of working life is a common idiom for monotonous toil.

clue.text: Support saving breadcrumbs for bird

indicators.note: saving means keeping hold of, so the support encloses the crumbled bread

parts.note: a rest is a prop or support
read as bread in crumbs: the letters of bread broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Put out a stand holding breadcrumbs to feed the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breadcrumbs' does double duty: its first part gives the letters and 'crumbs' breaks them up before they go inside the support.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the robin, from the red feathers on its chest.

clue.text: Liberal translation of writing system

indicators.note: a translation renders words in a new form, so the letters of liberal are reordered

explanation.surface: A loose rendering of a script.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactile script of raised dots read by touch, used by blind people.

clue.text: Schoolmaster's first sign about new items in lunch boxes

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word schoolmaster's
about means around, so the zodiac sign wraps the new letter

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: The headmaster's first signal about fresh items in packed lunches.
explanation.walkthrough: SARNIES is British slang for sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwiches are the staple contents of a packed lunch.

clue.text: Light cattle eating primarily dandelion leaves

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the cattle word holds the initial letters

parts.note: kine is an old plural for cows or cattle

indicators.note: primarily means at first, taking the opening letters of dandelion and leaves

explanation.surface: Pale cows munching dandelion leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a verb, to set alight, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to, as with kindling for a fire.

clue.text: Almost stop ruler after game?

indicators.note: after places the ruler's word following the shortened stop
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for stop is dropped

parts.note: to stall is to stop or come to a halt
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch nearly brings a contest to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'game' is hunted animals: pursuing them quietly is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Creeping up on deer or other quarry is a field sport, so it is a kind of game pursuit.

clue.text: Bachelor wearing smart watch chain

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the smart word goes round the bachelor

parts.note: smart in the sense of quick-witted means alert

explanation.surface: A single man sporting a stylish timepiece on a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian style of pocket-watch fob chain, named after Prince Albert.

clue.text: How to greet the Queen in shady part of garden?

parts.note: one greets royalty with a bow
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The right way to greet the monarch in the garden's shady corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy arbour or shelter in a garden, shaded by trees or climbing plants.

clue.text: Master invited graduate and two lecturers to dance

parts.note: asked means invited
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
L is an abbreviation for lecturer, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A college master asks a graduate and two dons to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal dance where guests wear masks to hide their identity.

clue.text: Old politician's hot in synthetic headgear

indicators.note: in places the hot letter inside the headgear word

parts.note: a wig is artificial hair worn on the head
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A former statesman sweats under his false hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the British party that preceded the Liberals, rivals of the Tories.

clue.text: Nasty round scarlet snake

parts.note: mean means unkind or nasty

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the colour is read backwards

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A vicious red snake coiled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake' is a verb here, to wind about, not the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to wind or wander along a twisting course, like a river.

clue.text: Correct uniform for sappers

indicators.note: for here means in front of, so the sappers' letters lead and the uniform word follows

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
dress is formal or military attire, as in full dress uniform

explanation.surface: The proper kit for military engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are the British Army's engineering corps; its soldiers are nicknamed sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: To put right a wrong or set a balance straight, as a verb.
